To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the South as an aggregate cannot speed up its rate of growth through export promotion; that the terms of trade of the South as a result of technical progress in the South are declining; that the terms-of-trade impact of Northern technical progress is negligible; that the terms or trade of the South is not affected by the monopoly power of Northern capitalists; that the South as whole cannot speed up the growth rate of the South through export promotion; and that the North-South model has a unique solution.
(i) the South cannot speed up its rate of growth through export promotion, and that (ii) the South can speed up its rate through import substitution.

the North-South trade is characterized by the following: (1) The monopoly power of the capitalists is not related to the terms of trade; (2) Technical progress in the North is not associated with the terms of trade, but technical progress in the South is; (3) The terms of trade are not related to the growth rate of the North; and (4) The South faces a terms oftrade loss if it tries to speed up its growth by means of export promotion.

the North-South growth rate relationship is not a simple one.
the North-South model has the same characteristics as the Kaldor model of the world.
there is no simple relationship between the monopoly powers of the North and the terms of trade, and that the South as whole cannot speed up long-term growth through export promotion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the South should not rely on the North for its growth and that it should not rely on its own export promotion for growth.
the North-South model is not a Kaldorian model.
, if the North is the only region to grow, then the South will not benefit from this growth in terms of its own long-term growth rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the North-South growth relationship is a two-way relationship.
the North-South trade is a zero-sum game in the sense that there are winners and losers.
a North-South trade model can be built on the lines of Kaldorian analysis, which has so far been confined to a closed economy.
